# Container DNS surface area

Scope: name resolution inside a container on a user-defined network, whatever the network's driver.
This covers the `/etc/resolv.conf` that the daemon writes for the container and the embedded
DNS resolver behind it, as observable from outside the daemon. In this spec, the user-defined
networks are the networks other than the predefined networks, ingress networks and
`docker_gwbridge`. On a Swarm-scoped network of a node-local driver, such as
`bridge`, the expectations hold for containers on the same node. Each node attaches its
containers to a network of its own, whose subnet can overlap the subnets on other nodes. On Linux
nodes, a `Links` alias of the querying container takes precedence over the records of its
networks, as [*DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE*](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE) says, and over forwarding. The other
expectations of this spec hold for a name, and for the `<name>` of a `<name>.<network>`
query, that is not such an alias.

This spec holds expectations that do not depend on any one driver. It is not yet a complete account.
[../README.md](../README.md) gives the model that this spec follows: the items of a spec, their
categories and what their verdicts depend on. [README.md](README.md) gives the conventions of the
networking specs, such as vantage points, daemon settings, timing and convergence ceilings, and host
requirements.

A container sends its DNS queries to the embedded DNS resolver, which is a DNS server that the
daemon runs for the container. The expectations state what the embedded resolver answers, and what
it forwards to upstream nameservers. A name resolves to an address when the embedded resolver
answers a DNS query for the name with that address. A container has external access when its default
route is on a network that is not `internal`, and replies to its egress traffic reach it. A
container on a bridge network whose `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` is
`false` does not have external access where [*BR-EGRESS-REPLY-DIRECT-ROUTING-OFF*](bridge-networking.md#BR-EGRESS-REPLY-DIRECT-ROUTING-OFF) applies. An
expectation that says that the embedded resolver forwards a query upstream does not cover a
container whose upstream nameservers are all the embedded resolver's own address, `127.0.0.11` on
a Linux node: a container created with `--dns` nameservers that are all that address, or
one created without `--dns` nameservers whose daemon's `dns` setting names
only that address. The host's `resolv.conf` is `/etc/resolv.conf`, also on a host that
runs systemd-resolved. An expectation that takes nameservers, search domains or options from the
host's `resolv.conf` takes them from that file as it is when the container starts, unless the
expectation says that the daemon reads it when the daemon started. Each start of the container reads
the file again and writes the container's `/etc/resolv.conf` again, also when a process in the
container has changed it.

On Linux nodes, the containers that follow do not use the embedded resolver, and nothing here
applies to them, other than the expectations whose state names the default bridge:

- A container attached only to the default bridge network, that has not had an endpoint on a
  user-defined network since it started.
- A container that uses the host's network.
- A container attached to the `none` network.

On Windows nodes, the expectations of this spec that state what the embedded resolver forwards, or
how it answers a query that it forwards, hold for a container whose endpoints are all on
`overlay` networks, or on `nat` networks created without
`com.docker.network.windowsshim.disable_gatewaydns` set to true.

<a id="container-dns-requirements"></a>

## Requirements

<a id="REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER**: User-defined networks use the embedded DNS server at 127.0.0.11

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/configure-dns.md

*Refined by:* [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER), [DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY](#DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY), [DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER](#DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)

A container attached to a user-defined network uses Docker's embedded DNS server, whose address
is 127.0.0.11, and applications that need an explicit DNS server address can use it. It has no
IPv6 address. The IPv4 address works in IPv6-only containers too.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL**: Lookups the embedded DNS server cannot answer are forwarded upstream

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/27/#270; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/configure-dns.md

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES](#DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED) · *Violated by:* [DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)

The embedded DNS server forwards external DNS lookups, those it cannot resolve itself, to
upstream DNS servers. On Windows it does so by default.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL**: Internal-only containers use DNS servers on their networks, not external

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-mq39-4gv4-mvpx; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/26.0/#2600; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/26.1/#2613

*Refines:* [PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS](../principles.md#PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS) · *Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL), [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER), [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER) · *Violated by:* [DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS)

For a container connected only to internal networks, the daemon does not forward requests to
external DNS servers, even when the host's server is on a loopback address. DNS servers within
an internal network stay usable.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE**: --dns servers are queried from the container, host servers from the host

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/28/#2800

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS](#DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS), [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT)

Requests to --dns servers are forwarded from the container's network namespace, so
--dns=127.0.0.1 is the container's own loopback. Nameservers read from the host's
/etc/resolv.conf are always accessed from the host's network namespace.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER**: Upstream servers are tried in order until a success or NXDOMAIN

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/18.03/#18031-ce; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/24.0/#2401

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-FAILOVER](#DNS-FWD-FAILOVER), [DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED](#DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED)

On a custom network the embedded DNS server queries upstream servers in order and stops after a
successful or NXDOMAIN response. A SERVFAIL moves on to the next server, and an NXDOMAIN is
returned to the client as NXDOMAIN.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-REFUSED"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-REFUSED**: A REFUSED from an upstream server moves on to the next server

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/libnetwork/pull/2171: a maintainer's merged change and its commit message

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-FAILOVER](#DNS-FWD-FAILOVER)

The embedded DNS server queries the next upstream server after a REFUSED response, as it does
after a SERVFAIL.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS**: With ndots set above 0, an unknown single-label name is not forwarded

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* moby/moby daemon/libnetwork/resolver.go: code comment on ndots in the forwarding path

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS) · *Violated by:* [DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS), [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)

When the user sets ndots above 0 and an A or AAAA query is for a name in the root domain, a
single-label name, that the embedded resolver cannot answer from its records, the resolver does
not forward it. It answers without an address and lets the client retry with a search domain
attached.

<a id="REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS**: Upstream servers come from --dns, else the daemon's dns, else the host

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/dockerd/#daemon-dns-options; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/28/#2800; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/26.1/#2613

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT) · *Violated by:* [DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM), [DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS)

By default containers use the same DNS servers as the host, from its /etc/resolv.conf. --dns
overrides them for a container, and the daemon's dns setting sets them for all containers. The
embedded DNS server ignores its own address when it is given as an upstream server.

<a id="REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER**: A live restore keeps the embedded resolver's configuration for running containers

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/libnetwork/pull/1620; moby/moby daemon/libnetwork/sandbox_store.go: code comment on sbState.ExtDNS

*Refined by:* [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM) · *Violated by:* [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)

After the daemon restarts with live-restore, the embedded resolver of a container that kept
running forwards queries as it did before the restart.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS**: A network alias resolves on its network, a shared one to every holder

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/network/connect/#alias; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/work-with-networks.md; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/prior-releases/#1110-2016-04-13

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER), [DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED](#DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED), [DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE](#DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

A network alias given with --network-alias or docker network connect --alias resolves to the
container on the network where it is defined. Several containers can share an alias on a
network; the answer then carries the records of all of them, and which of them comes first
varies between answers (DNS round robin).

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS**: A container name resolves before a search domain is tried

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Users who reach containers by single-label names on hosts whose search domains answer for many names (wildcard records or NXDOMAIN redirection). They rely on the name resolving to the container without knowing that ndots decides the order of the lookups

*Refined by:* [DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH](#DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)

In a container whose resolv.conf gets no valid ndots, neither from the container's or the
daemon's DNS options nor from the host's resolv.conf, a single-label name that the embedded
resolver has records for resolves to the container. This holds when a search domain of the
container has a record for that name too.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE**: Container names and aliases resolve whatever the case of the query

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/21169; https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/28689

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-CASE) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

The embedded DNS server matches names case-insensitively, as DNS does (RFC 4343).

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME**: Containers on a user-defined network resolve each other by name

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#differences-between-user-defined-bridges-and-the-default-bridge; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#user-defined-networks; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#name

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-AAAA](#DNS-NAMES-AAAA), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME](#DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME), [SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL), [SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL-BEFORE-HEALTHY](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-NODE-LOCAL-BEFORE-HEALTHY) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES), [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

On a user-defined network, containers can reach each other by container name through automatic
DNS resolution, unlike on the default bridge network.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES**: DNSNames lists an endpoint's DNS names, qualified as <name>.<network>

*Source kind:* api · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/reference/api/engine/version/v1.54/#tag/Container/operation/ContainerInspect; api/openapi.yaml: definition EndpointSettings (DNSNames)

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP), [DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME](#DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

The API's DNSNames lists all DNS names a container has on a network: its name, network aliases,
short ID and hostname. Appending .<network-name> to one of them gives its fully qualified form.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC**: Names follow connects, disconnects, starts, stops and renames

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#differences-between-user-defined-bridges-and-the-default-bridge; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/work-with-networks.md; https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/22466: a rename whose new name did not resolve that maintainers treated as a bug

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-CONNECT](#DNS-NAMES-CONNECT), [DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT](#DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME), [DNS-NAMES-EXIT](#DNS-NAMES-EXIT), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM), [DNS-NAMES-START](#DNS-NAMES-START), [DNS-NAMES-STOP](#DNS-NAMES-STOP), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER), [SWARM-SD-RENAME](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-RENAME) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

Containers can be connected to and disconnected from user-defined networks on the fly, and name
resolution follows: names and aliases stop resolving after a disconnect or stop, and resolve
again after a start. A renamed container resolves by its new name.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS**: A link alias resolves only for the container that has the link

*Source kind:* docs-history · *Source:* https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/configure-dns.md; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/work-with-networks.md

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)

--link=CONTAINER:ALIAS on a user-defined network gives the embedded DNS server an extra name
ALIAS for that container, and the lookup result is local to the container that has the link.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE**: Names resolve only among containers that share a network

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#differences-between-user-defined-bridges-and-the-default-bridge; https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/#use-user-defined-bridge-networks; https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/0e064795f2b8996655643315ab6ba82d72594e8a/engine/userguide/networking/work-with-networks.md

*Refines:* [PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS](../principles.md#PRIN-LEAST-ACCESS) · *Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK](#DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED), [DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK](#DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

A container's names and aliases are scoped to the networks it is attached to: containers on
those networks resolve them, containers on other networks do not, and a container attached to
several networks resolves the names on each of them.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES**: The embedded DNS server answers A, AAAA, PTR and MX for its names

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/prior-releases/#1110-2016-04-13; https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/18.02/#18020-ce; https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/21562

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-AAAA](#DNS-NAMES-AAAA), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING), [DNS-NAMES-MX](#DNS-NAMES-MX), [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

The embedded DNS server answers AAAA queries (IPv6 service discovery) as well as A queries,
reverse (PTR) queries for container addresses, and MX queries, for the names it has records for.

<a id="REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT**: An MX query for a known name gets an empty NOERROR answer

*Source kind:* issue · *Source:* moby/moby daemon/libnetwork/resolver.go: code comment in handleMXQuery

*Refined by:* [DNS-NAMES-MX](#DNS-NAMES-MX) · *Violated by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE), [DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)

When the embedded resolver resolves a name, it answers an MX query for that name with an empty
list and NOERROR, so that email clients can treat the name as an implicit MX (RFC 5321 section
5.1) and issue an A or AAAA query for it.

<a id="REQ-DNS-PORT53-SERVER"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-PORT53-SERVER**: A process in a container can serve DNS on port 53

*Source kind:* observable · *Source:* Users who run DNS servers such as dnsmasq or Pi-hole or AdGuard Home or CoreDNS or unbound in containers on user-defined networks. These servers bind port 53 on the wildcard address by default

*Refined by:* [DNS-PORT53-BIND](#DNS-PORT53-BIND)

A process in a container on a user-defined network can bind TCP and UDP port 53, on the wildcard
address too. The container's queries to 127.0.0.11 still reach the embedded resolver.

<a id="REQ-DNS-RESOLV-EDITABLE"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-RESOLV-EDITABLE**: A container's resolv.conf is editable at runtime

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/release-notes/prior-releases/#120-2014-08-20

*Refined by:* [DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT](#DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT)

/etc/resolv.conf is editable at runtime inside the container.

<a id="REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT**: A search domain of . sets no search domain

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/e5ef05054cb2215f5256cef460fd01f47091b04a/man/docker-run.1.md: the --dns-search flag help; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/c61fa33c23330b134e4107b138d3141424c8dc22/docs/userguide/networking/default_network/configure-dns.md: the --dns-search entry of its options table; moby/moby daemon/pkg/opts/opts.go: code comment on ValidateDNSSearch that validates the daemon's dns-search and reads a dot as a zero-length domain

*Refined by:* [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT), [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT-ONLY](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT-ONLY)

A search domain of . given with --dns-search or in the daemon's dns-search sets no search
domain: when it is the only search domain given, the container has none.

<a id="REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS"></a>

**Requirement REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS**: Search domains and DNS options come from the container, daemon or host

*Source kind:* docs · *Source:* https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/#dns-services; https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/dockerd/#daemon-dns-options

*Refined by:* [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR), [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST), [DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN](#DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN), [DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST](#DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST), [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR), [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON), [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST) · *Violated by:* [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE)

A container gets the search domains and DNS options given with --dns-search and --dns-opt;
otherwise those set for all containers in the daemon's dns-search and dns-opts; otherwise it
inherits the settings in the host's /etc/resolv.conf.

<a id="container-dns-rationales"></a>

## Rationales

<a id="RAT-DNS-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-NAMESPACE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-NAMESPACE**: The daemon's dns nameservers are reached from each container's namespace

*Rationale of:* [DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS](#DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS)

The daemon's `dns` setting gives every container that has no `--dns`
nameservers the same upstream nameservers. The embedded resolver queries them from each
container's network namespace, as it queries `--dns` nameservers, so a loopback
address in the setting is each container's own loopback, not the host's. A move to the host's
network namespace would send the queries of every container that the setting covers to a service
on the host in place of one in the container, at once, and a move back would do the reverse. It
should be made as a decision.

<a id="RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE**: A host resolv.conf that cannot be read as a file fails at the start, or at the first query

*Rationale of:* [DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-FIFO](#DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-FIFO), [DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-NOT-REGULAR](#DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-NOT-REGULAR)

The daemon reads the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` to find the upstream servers of a container
that uses the embedded resolver. A directory, a socket or a FIFO at that path cannot be read as
a file. Today the read's error, or a read that does not return, stops the container's start or
the daemon's own. The other choice is to treat the path as a file without nameservers, as
[*DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE*](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE) states for a missing file. The container then starts, and
the embedded resolver forwards to the loopback addresses in the host's network namespace, where
a resolver may not listen. One choice fails at the start. The other fails later, at the
container's first query for a name that the embedded resolver has no record for. A change from
one to the other should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-DNS-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE**: A link alias is the linking container's own name for a container

*Rationale of:* [DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE)

A link alias names the container that the linking container chose. Today it wins over every name
and network alias on that container's networks, so the linking container reaches the same
container whatever other containers join those networks. If network names won instead, a
container that joined later with the alias as its name would take the linking container's
traffic. A change to that order should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE**: A later rewrite of a running container's resolv.conf would replace edits made in the container

*Rationale of:* [DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED](#DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED), [DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT)

Once the embedded resolver has started for a container, the daemon does not write the
container's `/etc/resolv.conf` again while the container runs. From then on, the file and
the resolver do not follow the container's networks: a container that leaves its last
user-defined network keeps `nameserver 127.0.0.11`, and the resolver keeps answering
there. A process in the container can edit the file while the container runs. A daemon that
wrote the file again, for example to restore the host's nameservers after such a disconnect,
would replace those edits. It would also have to stop the resolver at the same moment, or leave
the file and the resolver in disagreement. When the daemon writes the file should change by
decision.

<a id="RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT**: The rcode and flags of a response decide what the client does next

*Rationale of:* [DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL), [DNS-FWD-OTHER-RCODE-RETURNED](#DNS-FWD-OTHER-RCODE-RETURNED), [DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-TRUNCATED](#DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-TRUNCATED)

The response that the embedded resolver gives decides how a client's lookup goes on. The TC bit
sends the client to TCP, where it gets every address ([*DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE*](#DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE)).
`SERVFAIL` reads as a temporary failure, which clients retry or take to another resolver.
Another rcode passed through from a nameserver ends the lookup with that nameserver's verdict. A
change to which response a client gets in these cases changes how its lookups end, and should be
deliberate.

<a id="RAT-DNS-NO-UPSTREAM-LEFT"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-NO-UPSTREAM-LEFT**: When no configured upstream is left, a fallback would send queries to servers that nobody configured

*Rationale of:* [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY)

The embedded resolver does not forward to a configured nameserver `127.0.0.11`
([*DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF*](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF), [*DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON*](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON)). When that is the
container's only nameserver, no upstream is left. Three outcomes are possible for a name without
records: `SERVFAIL`, as today; a fallback to the host's nameservers; or a query that the
resolver forwards to itself. A fallback would send the container's queries to servers that its
configuration does not name, and a loop would hold every such query until it times out. The
choice among the three should be made on purpose.

<a id="RAT-DNS-OTHER-TYPES-LEAVE-THE-NODE"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-OTHER-TYPES-LEAVE-THE-NODE**: For a name on the network, the resolver's choice for other query types decides which queries go upstream

*Rationale of:* [DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED](#DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED)

The embedded resolver answers a name that it has address records for itself only for A, AAAA and
MX queries. A query of another type, for a name that it has records for, takes the path of a
query for a name without records ([*DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME*](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME)): it goes upstream. An empty
answer from the resolver itself is as defensible, because the name belongs to the container's
network. The two differ for a name that exists both on the network and upstream: today its
addresses come from the network and every other record from upstream. They also differ in
whether queries that carry the names of containers and aliases leave the node. A change to that
split, in either direction, should be deliberate.

<a id="RAT-DNS-TTL-STALE-ADDRESSES"></a>

**Rationale RAT-DNS-TTL-STALE-ADDRESSES**: The TTL sets how long a client may keep an address that no longer belongs to the name

*Rationale of:* [DNS-NAMES-TTL](#DNS-NAMES-TTL)

The TTL of an answer from the embedded resolver's own records is the time for which a client or
a caching resolver in the container may keep using an address after the container behind the
name stops, restarts with another address, or is replaced. A longer TTL lengthens that time. A
shorter one sends more queries to the resolver. The value trades one against the other, and a
change to it should be a decision about that trade.

<a id="container-dns-host-requirements"></a>

## Host requirements

The kernel facilities and programs hold on Linux nodes. The host configuration holds on Linux and
Windows nodes. The conventions for this section are in [README.md](README.md#readme-host-requirements).
The embedded resolver needs NAT rules in the container's network namespace under the active firewall
backend. It needs them whether or not the daemon's `iptables` setting is true.

`NFT_NAT`.

<a id="container-dns-host-configuration"></a>

### Host configuration

<a id="DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS"></a>

**Host requirement DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS**: Host nameservers that the node reaches and that resolve the queried names

*Platforms:* linux, windows · *Kind:* config

*Needed by:* [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM), [DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES](#DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT), [SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAME-UPSTREAM](swarm-traffic.md#SWARM-SD-SERVICE-NAME-UPSTREAM)

*Facility:* Host nameservers that the node reaches, and that resolve the names that an
expectation queries, such as public names. On a Linux node, these are the nameservers in the
host's `resolv.conf`. On a Windows node, these are the nameservers in the DNS server list
that the Host Networking Service gives the container's endpoint, other than the endpoint's
gateway address, where the embedded resolver listens. A nameserver on a network that the node
shares with it meets this as well as one on the internet.

*Needed when:* A query that the embedded resolver forwards to the host's nameservers

<a id="container-dns-file-resolv-conf"></a>

## `resolv.conf`

This section holds on Linux nodes. Its expectations, other than the expectation about a process's
changes to the file, hold for a `/etc/resolv.conf` that has not changed since the daemon wrote
it.

A container's DNS options are the options that it was created with. If it was created without DNS
options, they are the daemon's `dns-opts`. The options in effect are the container's
DNS options when it has any. Otherwise, they are the options in the host's `resolv.conf`. A
valid `ndots` is an integer of 0 or more.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-NAMESERVER**: The resolv.conf nameserver is 127.0.0.11

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

The `/etc/resolv.conf` nameserver is `127.0.0.11`. The file names no other nameserver,
IPv4 or IPv6.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY**: In an IPv6-only container, 127.0.0.11 answers for names on its networks

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS))

*Applies to:* A container whose user-defined networks all have `EnableIPv4` false and
`EnableIPv6` true, and another container on one of those networks, with IPv6 enabled
in its network namespace and on its interfaces on those networks, where no endpoint on those
networks other than that container's has that container's name or a name that differs from it
only in the case of its letters

The `/etc/resolv.conf` nameserver is `127.0.0.11`. An AAAA query that the container
sends to `127.0.0.11` for the other container's name gets that container's IPv6 address on one
of those networks.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-CTR**: resolv.conf has the ndots from the container's DNS options

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options include a valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the `ndots` value from the container's DNS options. A
value above 15 is kept as given.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST**: Without DNS options, resolv.conf has the host's ndots

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE))

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options are empty, and a host `resolv.conf` with a
valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the `ndots` value from the host's `resolv.conf`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-NO-HOST**: With container DNS options, resolv.conf has no host option they lack

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose DNS options include any option, and a host `resolv.conf`
with an option that the container's DNS options do not include, such as `edns0`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has no option that the host's `resolv.conf` has and the
container's DNS options do not, apart from an `ndots:0` that the daemon adds when
the container's DNS options set no valid `ndots`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH**: Without ndots, a container name resolves before the search domains

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS) · *Exact form:* [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE))

*Applies to:* A container whose options in effect do not include a valid `ndots`,
with a search domain `<domain>` in its `/etc/resolv.conf`, and an upstream nameserver
that has a record for `<name>.<domain>`, where `<name>` is a single-label name that
the embedded resolver has records for

A lookup of `<name>` in the container, through a resolver that follows its
`/etc/resolv.conf`, such as the C library's, gets the addresses in the embedded resolver's
records for `<name>`. It does not get the address of `<name>.<domain>`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO**: Without a valid ndots in effect, resolv.conf has options ndots:0

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH](#DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)

*Applies to:* A container whose options in effect do not include a valid `ndots`

`/etc/resolv.conf` contains `options ndots:0`. This applies when the options
do not set `ndots`, and when all of the `ndots` values in them are
invalid.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-CTR**: resolv.conf has the container's search domains

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container created with search domains

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search domains that the container was created with, other than
`.`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DAEMON**: Without its own search domains, resolv.conf has the daemon's dns-search

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container created without search domains, and a daemon with
`dns-search` set

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search domains in the daemon's `dns-search`, other
than `.`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST**: Without any dns-search, resolv.conf has the host's search list

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE))

*Applies to:* A container created without search domains, and a daemon without
`dns-search`

`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search list from the host's `resolv.conf`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT**: A search domain of . is left out of resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

`/etc/resolv.conf` does not contain a search domain of `.` given with
`--dns-search` or in the daemon's `dns-search`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT-ONLY**: With . as the only search domain, resolv.conf has no search line

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-DOT) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose only search domain, given with `--dns-search` or in
the daemon's `dns-search`, is `.`

`/etc/resolv.conf` does not have a `search` line, even if the host's
`resolv.conf` has one.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN**: Apart from ndots, resolv.conf lists the options as given

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE))

Apart from `ndots`, `/etc/resolv.conf` lists the options in effect as they
were given.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-SOURCE**: A bridge-mode container gets search and options from systemd's resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH](#DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH), [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-HOST), [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO), [DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN](#DNS-RESOLV-OPTIONS-AS-GIVEN), [DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST](#DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-HOST) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-SEARCH-OPTIONS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` named only `127.0.0.53` when the daemon
started, and a container that has an endpoint on a user-defined network, from its start or after
a connect, and whose `HostConfig.NetworkMode` is the default bridge, such as a
container that `POST /containers/create` created without a `NetworkMode`,
even when its `EndpointsConfig` names only a user-defined network, or the container
of a service task whose first network is not one of the Swarm's predefined networks

When neither the container nor the daemon gives search domains, the container's
`/etc/resolv.conf` has the search list of `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf`. Where
the search list of the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` differs from it, the container's file
does not have that list. When the container's DNS options are empty, the container's file has
the options of `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` other than an invalid
`ndots`, with an `ndots:0` added when they set no valid
`ndots`. Apart from that `ndots:0`, it has no option of the host's
`/etc/resolv.conf` that `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` lacks.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-CTR-EDIT-KEPT**: A process's change to resolv.conf is kept, across connects too

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-RESOLV-EDITABLE](#REQ-DNS-RESOLV-EDITABLE) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container, also one attached only to the default bridge network

After a process in the container changes the container's `/etc/resolv.conf`, the file
keeps the process's content while the container runs. A connect or disconnect of the container
does not change the file. This includes a connect of a container that was attached only to the
default bridge network to a user-defined network.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT**: After a connect from the default bridge, the container resolves names

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER), [REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE](#REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE), [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge on a systemd-resolved host, queries skip 127.0.0.53 ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM))

*Applies to:* A running container attached only to the default bridge, created without
`--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting, and
whose `/etc/resolv.conf` has not changed since the daemon wrote it

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a user-defined network responds 200, the
container resolves the names of the containers on that network. The embedded resolver forwards
the queries that [*DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME*](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME) says it forwards upstream to the nameservers in
the host's `resolv.conf`, loopback nameservers included. It queries them from the host's
network namespace.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-NAMESERVER**: After a connect from the default bridge, the nameserver is 127.0.0.11

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container attached only to the default bridge, whose
`/etc/resolv.conf` has not changed since the daemon wrote it

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a user-defined network responds 200, the
`/etc/resolv.conf` nameserver is `127.0.0.11`.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED**: resolv.conf is not rewritten once the embedded resolver starts

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pinned by:* [DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT), [DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START](#DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A later rewrite of a running container's resolv.conf would replace edits made in the container ([RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE](#RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE))

After the embedded resolver starts for a container, `/etc/resolv.conf` does not change
again while the container runs. After a disconnect of the container from its last user-defined
network, the file still names the embedded resolver's address as its nameserver.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-USER-DEFINED-START**: A container started on a user-defined network keeps its resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED](#DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that started with an endpoint on a user-defined network

The container's `/etc/resolv.conf` keeps the content that it had at start. This holds
after later connects and disconnects. After a disconnect of the container from its last
user-defined network, the file still names the embedded resolver's address as its nameserver.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-UNCHANGED-AFTER-CONNECT**: After a connect from the default bridge, resolv.conf stops changing

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED](#DNS-RESOLV-NOT-UPDATED) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that started attached only to the default bridge, and that a
later connect attached to a user-defined network

The container's `/etc/resolv.conf` keeps the content that it had after that connect. This
holds after later connects and disconnects. After a disconnect of the container from its last
user-defined network, the file still names the embedded resolver's address as its nameserver.

<a id="DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-RESOLV-RESOLVER-AFTER-DISCONNECT**: The embedded resolver keeps answering after the last disconnect

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A later rewrite of a running container's resolv.conf would replace edits made in the container ([RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE](#RAT-DNS-RESOLV-WRITTEN-ONCE))

*Applies to:* A running container that has had an endpoint on a user-defined network at any time
since it started

After the container disconnects from every user-defined network, the embedded resolver continues
to answer the container's queries.

<a id="container-dns-names-and-answers"></a>

## Names and answers

In this section, the querying container is the container that sends the DNS query. The embedded
resolver has records for a name on a network when an endpoint on that network has that name. On an
overlay network, the endpoint of a service's task counts only while the task is running, as
[Service discovery](swarm-traffic.md#swarm-traffic-service-discovery) in [swarm-traffic.md](swarm-traffic.md) defines it. An
endpoint's names are its container's name, short ID and hostname, and its network aliases. On a
Linux node, the names of an endpoint on the default bridge are instead the names, if any, that
`NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` lists for its container. An endpoint on an
ingress network, and the endpoint that the daemon adds on `docker_gwbridge` for a
container's gateway, have no names. An endpoint also has every name that differs from one of these
only in the case of its letters. An expectation about a name holds where, on the querying
container's networks, no endpoint other than the one that the expectation names has that name,
unless the expectation names that case. In `<name>.<network>`, `<name>` stands for a
name and `<network>` for the name of a network. Both are placeholders, not literal text. On a
Swarm-scoped network of a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`, a request's effect on what
containers on other nodes resolve holds within the ceiling that the timing rules in [README.md](README.md#readme-timing) give it.

An expectation in this section names `none` when the embedded DNS resolver answers the query from
its own records. It does this the same way on every platform.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME**: A container's name resolves to its address on a shared network

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network that it shares with
the querying container, where no other network of the querying container has an endpoint with
that container's name

The container's name resolves to its address on the shared network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CASE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-CASE**: Names and aliases resolve whatever the case of the query

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network that it shares with
the querying container

Its name and its network aliases resolve whatever the case of the query: a container named
`Web` resolves as `web` and as `WEB`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ALIAS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ALIAS**: A network alias resolves on its network only

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A network alias given to a container's endpoint, where no other network of the
querying container has an endpoint with that alias

The alias resolves to the container's address on that network, for containers on that network
only.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED**: An alias that several containers share resolves to all of them

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* Several containers on a network whose endpoints have the same network alias, where
no other network of the querying container has an endpoint with that alias

The alias resolves to the addresses of all of those containers on that network. Over UDP, this
holds when the answer fits in 512 bytes, or in the query's EDNS0 buffer size when that is
larger.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME**: A container's short ID and hostname resolve as its name does

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

A container's short ID (the first 12 hex digits of its ID) and its hostname resolve as its name
does.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES**: DNSNames lists the name, aliases, short ID and hostname, which all resolve

*Observed from:* api, ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES) · *Exact form:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network

`GET /containers/{id}/json` lists in
`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` the container's name, the aliases of
its endpoint on that network, its short ID and its hostname. Each of them resolves on that
network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-SHORT-ID**: DNSNames lists the name, the aliases, the short ID, then the hostname

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network

`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json`
lists the container's name, then the aliases of its endpoint on that network, then the
container's short ID and then its hostname. It does not list a name more than once.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME**: After a rename, DNSNames has the new name and not the old one

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED)

*Applies to:* A running container whose hostname and network aliases are not its name

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204,
`NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json`
has the new name for each user-defined network. It does not have the old name. It still lists
the aliases, the short ID and the hostname, and no other name.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE**: DNSNames on the default bridge is empty

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* After a rename, DNSNames on the default bridge lists names ([DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED)), DNSNames that a request gives for the default bridge are reported as given ([DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached to the default bridge

`NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json` is
empty.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-FILLED**: After a rename, DNSNames on the default bridge lists names

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Concerns:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-RENAME) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES)

*Applies to:* A running container attached to the default bridge

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container responds 204,
`NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` in `GET /containers/{id}/json`
lists the new name, the short ID and, when it differs from the short ID, the hostname. The list
stays after the container stops and starts again. A rename while the container is stopped does
not change it.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED**: DNSNames that a request gives for the default bridge are reported as given

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES)

`POST /containers/create` with `HostConfig.NetworkMode` `bridge` and a list
of names in `NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig.bridge.DNSNames` responds 201, and
`POST /networks/{id}/connect` that connects a container to the default bridge with such
a list in `EndpointConfig.DNSNames` responds 200. `GET /containers/{id}/json`
then reports that list in `NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames`, also when its
names are not the container's name, short ID or hostname. A start of the container does not
change the list.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK**: A name resolves if it exists on any of the querying container's networks

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE) · *Exact form:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

A name resolves when an endpoint with that name exists on any user-defined network that the
querying container is attached to.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-OTHER-NETWORK**: A query gets no address from a network the querying container is not on

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

A query for a name does not get the address of an endpoint on a network that the querying
container is not attached to. This holds also when an endpoint on one of the querying
container's networks has that name.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-START"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-START**: After a start, a container's name and aliases resolve on its networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A created or stopped standalone container

After `POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds 204, its name and its
aliases on each of its user-defined networks resolve for the other containers on that network.
This holds whether or not the container has a healthcheck.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-CONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-CONNECT**: After a connect, a container's name and aliases resolve on the network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A running standalone container

After `POST /networks/{id}/connect` to a user-defined network for the container responds
200, its name and its aliases on that network resolve for the other containers on the network.
This holds whether or not the container has a healthcheck.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-DISCONNECT**: After a disconnect, a container's name and aliases stop resolving there

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A running container with an endpoint on a user-defined network

After `POST /networks/{id}/disconnect` for the container from that network responds 200,
the other containers on that network do not resolve its name or aliases to its address on that
network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-STOP"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-STOP**: After a stop, a container's name and aliases stop resolving

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A running container with endpoints on user-defined networks

After `POST /containers/{id}/stop` for the container responds 204, the other containers
on each of those networks do not resolve its name or aliases to its address on that network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-EXIT"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-EXIT**: After its process exits, a container's name and aliases stop resolving

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows
