*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-ALLOCATION), [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT)

*Applies to:* A running container with endpoints on user-defined networks, whose restart policy
does not restart it

After the daemon emits the container's `die` event, whether its process exited or
`POST /containers/{id}/kill` ended it, the other containers on each of those networks do
not resolve its name or aliases to its address on that network. On a network that is not
Swarm-scoped, this holds once the daemon emits the event.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-RENAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-RENAME**: After a rename, the new name resolves and the old one does not

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES)

*Applies to:* A running container whose hostname and network aliases differ from its name in
more than the case of their letters

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container, with a new name that differs
from its old name in more than the case of its letters, responds 204, its new name resolves and
its old name does not resolve to its address, for containers on each of its user-defined
networks on its node.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES**: A default-bridge container's names do not resolve to its default-bridge address

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* After a rename, default-bridge names resolve on a user-defined network ([DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, a running container attached only to the default
bridge, created and started without `DNSNames` for it, and another container attached
to the default bridge and to a user-defined network

The other container does not resolve the first container's name, short ID or hostname to the
first container's address on the default bridge.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-RENAME-RESOLVES**: After a rename, default-bridge names resolve on a user-defined network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES) · *Concerns:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, a running container attached to the default bridge,
and another container attached to the default bridge and to a user-defined network

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the first container responds 204, the other
container resolves the new name and the short ID to the renamed container's address on the
default bridge. After the renamed container stops and starts again, the other container resolves
the names that `NetworkSettings.Networks.bridge.DNSNames` then lists to the renamed
container's address on the default bridge.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED-RESOLVES**: Names requested for the default bridge resolve on a user-defined network

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerns:* [DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-NO-NAMES), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-REQUESTED) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME)

*Applies to:* A node that is not in a Swarm, a running container attached only to the default
bridge, created with `HostConfig.NetworkMode` `bridge` and a list of names that
includes its name in `NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig.bridge.DNSNames`, and another
container attached to the default bridge and to a user-defined network

The other container resolves each name in that list, the first container's name included, to
the first container's address on the default bridge.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS**: A and AAAA queries for a known name are answered from its records

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A query gets no address when the first network lacks that family ([DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

The embedded resolver answers an A or AAAA query for a name that it has records for from those
records. This holds for a single-label name too, whatever `ndots` is set by the
options in effect, which the [resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf) section defines.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER-FAMILY-MISSING**: A query gets no address when the first network lacks that family

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES)

*Applies to:* A Linux node, and a name that several of the querying container's networks have
records for, where the first of those networks that the embedded resolver consults has no
address of one family for the name and another of them has one. On a node that is not in a
Swarm, the embedded resolver consults the networks in the order that
[*DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER*](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER) gives. On a node in a Swarm, it consults the Swarm-scoped
networks other than the ingress network first, then the ingress network, then the networks that
are not Swarm-scoped, and this expectation covers a name that, in the first of these groups that
has records for it, only one network has records for.

An A or AAAA query for the name, of that family, gets an empty `NOERROR` response.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-AAAA"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-AAAA**: An AAAA query returns the container's IPv6 address on a shared network

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A container with an IPv6 address on a user-defined network that it shares with the
querying container, where no other network of the querying container has an endpoint with that
container's name

An AAAA query for that name returns the container's IPv6 address on the shared network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING**: A query of the address type a name lacks is answered without an address

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Exact form:* [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* Records in the embedded resolver for a name that are all A records, or all AAAA
records, and an upstream nameserver of the container that has a record of the other type for
that name

A query of the other type for that name gets a response without an address. The embedded
resolver does not forward this query upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR**: A query of the address type a name lacks gets an empty NOERROR

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* Records in the embedded resolver for a name that are all A records, or all AAAA
records

A query of the other type for that name gets an empty `NOERROR` response.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-MX"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-MX**: An MX query for a known name gets an empty NOERROR response

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

An MX query for a name that the embedded resolver has A or AAAA records for gets an empty
`NOERROR` response. The embedded resolver does not forward this query upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPE-FORWARDED**: Other query types for a name with records are forwarded upstream

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Rationale:* For a name on the network, the resolver's choice for other query types decides which queries go upstream ([RAT-DNS-OTHER-TYPES-LEAVE-THE-NODE](#RAT-DNS-OTHER-TYPES-LEAVE-THE-NODE))

*Applies to:* A name that the embedded resolver has address records for, and a query type other
than A, AAAA and MX for which the first of the querying container's upstream nameservers has a
record for that name

The embedded resolver forwards upstream a query of a type other than A, AAAA and MX for a name
that it has address records for. The query gets that nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-ORDER**: Outside a Swarm, A and AAAA answers come from the first network only

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK](#DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS))

*Applies to:* A Linux node that is not in a Swarm

When several of the querying container's networks have records for a name, the embedded resolver
answers an A or AAAA query for that name from the records of the first network only. The order
is: (1) Endpoints with a higher `GwPriority` first. (2) Networks that are not
`internal` first. (3) Endpoints that give the container a gateway or a default route for more
IP versions first, whether or not the container's default route for a version goes through them.
(4) Network names in byte order. Each step orders only the endpoints that the steps before it
leave equal.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE**: Answers list all addresses unless the UDP size limit truncates them

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A network alias that the endpoints of several containers on one network share

Over UDP, an answer from the embedded resolver's own records lists all of the alias's addresses
on the network that it answers from when it fits in a size limit. The limit is the larger of 512
bytes and the query's EDNS0 buffer size. Over TCP, the answer lists all of those addresses.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-TRUNCATED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-TRUNCATED**: An answer over the UDP size limit is truncated with the TC bit set

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Rationale:* The rcode and flags of a response decide what the client does next ([RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT](#RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT))

Over UDP, when an answer from the embedded resolver's own records does not fit in the larger of
512 bytes and the query's EDNS0 buffer size, the embedded resolver truncates it and sets the TC
bit.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER**: Answers vary which of a shared alias's addresses comes first

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A network alias that the endpoints of several containers on one network share

Each answer from the embedded resolver's own records lists the alias's addresses in an order
chosen for that answer. For an alias with two addresses, each of them comes first in at least
one of 20 consecutive answers.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-TTL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-TTL**: Answers from the embedded resolver's records have a TTL of 600 seconds

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS)) · *Rationale:* The TTL sets how long a client may keep an address that no longer belongs to the name ([RAT-DNS-TTL-STALE-ADDRESSES](#RAT-DNS-TTL-STALE-ADDRESSES))

The records in an answer from the embedded resolver's own records have a TTL of 600 seconds.
This holds for A, AAAA and PTR answers.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-PTR**: Reverse lookups resolve the addresses of containers on shared networks

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Exact form:* [DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A reverse lookup matches only in lower case ([DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE)), Reverse lookups fail for IPv6 addresses with :: for 3+ groups at an end ([DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

Reverse (PTR) lookups resolve for the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of containers on the querying
container's user-defined networks.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP**: A reverse lookup's <name>.<network> resolves forward to the address

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS)

*Applies to:* A container's address whose reverse lookup returns `<name>.<network>.`,
where no network of the querying container has records for `<name>.<network>`

A forward lookup of `<name>.<network>` returns that address. This holds also when
another of the querying container's networks has records for `<name>`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN**: Reverse lookups fail for IPv6 addresses with :: for 3+ groups at an end

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES)

*Applies to:* A container with an IPv6 address on a user-defined network that it shares with the
querying container, where the address's text form (RFC 5952) starts or ends with `::` that
stands for three or more groups of zeros, such as `fd00:0:0:1:1::`

The embedded resolver does not answer a PTR query for that address from its records. It handles
the query as it handles a query for a name that it has no records for.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM**: A reverse lookup answers <name>.<network>. with the container name

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* A reverse lookup matches only in lower case ([DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE)), Reverse lookups fail for IPv6 addresses with :: for 3+ groups at an end ([DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-IPV6-ZERO-RUN)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

The answer to a reverse lookup of a container's address on a user-defined network is
`<name>.<network>.`, where `<name>` is the container's name and `<network>` is the
network's name. It is never an alias, the short ID or the hostname.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-PTR-CASE-SENSITIVE**: A reverse lookup matches only in lower case

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES)

The embedded resolver answers a PTR query for the address of a container on the querying
container's networks from its records only when the query's `in-addr.arpa` or
`ip6.arpa` suffix, and for an IPv6 address the hex digits of the name, are in lower
case. It handles a PTR query with an upper-case letter in them as it handles a query for a name
that it has no records for.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED**: <name>.<network> resolves to the addresses of <name> on that network

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* The network part of <name>.<network> matches only in its own case ([DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS)

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, and records for
`<name>` on that network, where no network of the querying container has records for
`<name>.<network>`

A query for `<name>.<network>` resolves to the addresses of `<name>` on that network
only. This holds also when another of the querying container's networks has records for
`<name>`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-CASE-SENSITIVE**: The network part of <name>.<network> matches only in its own case

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED) · *Concerns:* [DNS-NAMES-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-CASE) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES)

In a `<name>.<network>` query, `<network>` matches a network only when its case is
the same as the case of the network's name. The `<name>` part matches whatever its case.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WINDOWS**: On Windows, <name>.<network> is not answered from <name>'s records

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Concerns:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-ROUND-TRIP) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES)

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, and records for
`<name>` on that network, where no network of the querying container has records for
`<name>.<network>`, and a record of the query's type for `<name>.<network>`
on the first of the querying container's upstream nameservers

The embedded resolver on a Windows node does not answer a query for `<name>.<network>`
from the records of `<name>` on `<network>`. It forwards the query upstream. The query gets
that nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-NOT-ATTACHED**: <name>.<network> is forwarded when the querying container is not on it

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A network whose name is a valid DNS label and that the querying container is not
attached to, where no network of the querying container has records for
`<name>.<network>`, `<network>` being that network's name, and a record of the
query's type for `<name>.<network>` on the first of the querying container's upstream
nameservers

The embedded resolver forwards a query for `<name>.<network>` upstream. The query gets
that nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME**: An endpoint named <name>.<network> resolves by its whole name

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME) · *Exact form:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, where an endpoint is
named `<name>`, and records for `<name>.<network>` on one of the querying
container's networks

`<name>.<network>` resolves to the addresses in the records for the whole name.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY**: An endpoint named <name>.<network> wins over <name> on <network>

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Within:* [SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT](swarm-lifecycle.md#SWARM-CEIL-REASSIGNMENT) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)), On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records ([DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS](#DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS))

*Applies to:* A querying container attached to the network `<network>`, where an endpoint is
named `<name>`, and records for `<name>.<network>` on one of the querying
container's networks

`<name>.<network>` resolves only to the addresses in the records for the whole name.
It does not resolve to the address of `<name>` on the network `<network>`.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-WINDOWS-OTHER-DRIVERS**: On Windows, names on networks other than nat and overlay are not answered from records

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-AAAA](#DNS-NAMES-AAAA), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-ORDER), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-RECORDS), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING), [DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR](#DNS-NAMES-ADDRESS-TYPE-MISSING-NOERROR), [DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED](#DNS-NAMES-ALIAS-SHARED), [DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE](#DNS-NAMES-ANSWER-SIZE), [DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK](#DNS-NAMES-ANY-NETWORK), [DNS-NAMES-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-CASE), [DNS-NAMES-CONNECT](#DNS-NAMES-CONNECT), [DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [DNS-NAMES-MX](#DNS-NAMES-MX), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY), [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM), [DNS-NAMES-RENAME](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME), [DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME](#DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME), [DNS-NAMES-START](#DNS-NAMES-START), [DNS-NAMES-TTL](#DNS-NAMES-TTL) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES)

On a Windows node, the daemon gives the embedded resolver only to a container's endpoints on
`overlay` networks, and on `nat` networks other than one created with
`com.docker.network.windowsshim.disable_gatewaydns` set to true. On a user-defined
network of another driver, such as `transparent` or `l2bridge`, a query from a
container for the name of another container on the network is not answered from the daemon's
records: a query for a network alias of another container on the network does not resolve to
that container's address on the network.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS**: A link alias resolves to the linked container for the linking one only

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* A link alias matches only in its own case ([DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE)), After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with `<name>:<alias>` in the `Links` of
its endpoint settings for a user-defined network

The alias resolves to the named container's address on that network. It resolves only for
queries from the container that has the link.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-CASE**: A link alias matches only in its own case

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS](#DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS)

A query matches a link alias only when its case is the same as
the case of the alias in `Links`. The embedded resolver answers a query for the alias
in another case as it answers a name that is not a link alias: from the records of the querying
container's networks, or upstream.

<a id="DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE**: A link alias takes precedence over names on the querying container's networks

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* After a Swarm leave, running containers' names stop resolving ([DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS](#DNS-NAMES-SWARM-LEAVE-RECORDS)) · *Rationale:* A link alias is the linking container's own name for a container ([RAT-DNS-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE](#RAT-DNS-LINK-ALIAS-PRECEDENCE))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container with `<name>:<alias>` in the `Links` of
its endpoint settings for a user-defined network

The alias takes precedence over the names and network aliases on each of that container's
networks. It resolves to the named container even when another container on one of those
networks has the alias as its name or as a network alias.

### In a Swarm

<a id="DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM**: In a Swarm, a rename applies on a multi-host network on its own node

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DYNAMIC), [REQ-SWARM-SD-CONTAINER-NAME](swarm-traffic.md#REQ-SWARM-SD-CONTAINER-NAME) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS), [SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-BR-NETFILTER), [SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-FIREWALL-CLUSTER-PORTS), [SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-HNS-OVERLAY), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NETNS-VETH-BRIDGE), [SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-NFTABLES-ROUTE-CHAINS), [SWARM-HOST-VXLAN](swarm-networking.md#SWARM-HOST-VXLAN) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)

*Applies to:* A node in a Swarm, and a running container whose hostname and network aliases
differ from its name in more than the case of their letters, with an endpoint on a Swarm-scoped
network of a multi-host driver, such as `overlay`

After `POST /containers/{id}/rename` for the container, with a new name that differs
from its old name in more than the case of its letters, responds 204, its new name resolves and
its old name does not resolve to its address, for containers on that network on its node.

[REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE), On a node in a Swarm, `POST /containers/{id}/rename` changes the
container's records only on Swarm-scoped networks of multi-host drivers, such as `overlay`. It
does not change them on other networks, such as user-defined bridge networks and Swarm-scoped
networks of node-local drivers. The container's new name does not resolve there. Its old name
continues to resolve there after the rename, and a reverse lookup of its address there returns
the old name. The old name continues to resolve there after the container is removed.
