[DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME), [DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY](#DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-QUALIFIED-WHOLE-NAME-ONLY), [DNS-NAMES-PTR](#DNS-NAMES-PTR), [DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM](#DNS-NAMES-PTR-FORM), [DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME](#DNS-NAMES-SHORT-ID-HOSTNAME), [DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH](#DNS-RESOLV-CTR-NAME-BEFORE-SEARCH), [DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY](#DNS-RESOLV-IPV6-ONLY) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-EMBEDDED-RESOLVER), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-ALIAS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-BEFORE-SEARCH-DOMAINS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CASE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-CTR-NAME), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-DNSNAMES), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-LINK-ALIAS), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-MX-IMPLICIT), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-NETWORK-SCOPE), [REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES](#REQ-DNS-NAMES-QUERY-TYPES)

Take a node in a Swarm, whether it created the Swarm with `POST /swarm/init` or joined
it, that leaves it with `POST /swarm/leave`. After the leave, the names of the
containers that were running on the node's user-defined networks before the leave stop resolving
there, and so do reverse lookups of their addresses. The embedded resolver handles a query of
any type for one of those names, and a PTR query for one of their addresses, as it handles a
query for a name that no endpoint on the querying container's networks has. Link aliases for
those containers stop resolving too. A container that starts after the leave gets records that
resolve.

<a id="container-dns-forwarding"></a>

## Forwarding

<a id="DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-PUBLIC-NAMES**: Names without a record resolve through the host's nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE))

*Applies to:* A container that has external access and was created without `--dns`
nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting

A name that the embedded resolver has no record for resolves to the addresses that the host's
nameservers give for it, such as a public DNS name.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL**: An internal-only container never queries unreachable or host nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr, node, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL) · *Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached only to `internal` networks

No nameserver that the container cannot reach from its own network namespace receives the
container's queries, such as a nameserver set with `--dns` or in the daemon's
`dns` setting at an address that the node reaches and the container does not. The
embedded resolver also does not forward them to the nameservers in the host's
`resolv.conf`.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL**: Unknown names get SERVFAIL in an internal-only container without --dns

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names ([DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)), With ndots 0 or invalid, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR ([DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container attached only to `internal` networks and created
without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting

A query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for gets `SERVFAIL`.
When the options in effect set `ndots` to 1 or more, a single-label A or AAAA query
gets an empty `NOERROR` response instead.

<a id="DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS**: The embedded resolver forwards to the --dns nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS) · *Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container that has external access and was created with `--dns`
nameservers, and a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for, for which the
first nameserver set with `--dns` other than the embedded resolver's own address and
the host's nameservers give different addresses

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers set with `--dns`, other than its own
address (`127.0.0.11` on a Linux node, the network's gateway address on a Windows node), in
place of the host's nameservers. A query for that name resolves to the address that the first of
those `--dns` nameservers gives.

<a id="DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS**: Without --dns, the embedded resolver forwards to the daemon's dns

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux, os-windows · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS) · *Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with a `dns` setting, and a container that has external
access and was created without `--dns` nameservers, and a name that the embedded
resolver does not have a record for, for which the first nameserver in the daemon's
`dns` setting other than the embedded resolver's own address and the host's
nameservers give different addresses

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers in the daemon's `dns` setting,
other than its own address (`127.0.0.11` on a Linux node, the network's gateway address on a
Windows node), in place of the host's nameservers. A query for that name resolves to the address
that the first of those nameservers gives.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER**: An internal-only container resolves through a --dns nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS)

*Applies to:* A container attached only to `internal` networks and created with
`--dns` set to the address of a nameserver in another container on one of those
networks

The container created with `--dns` resolves names through that nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER**: An internal-only container resolves through the daemon's dns nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with a `dns` setting that holds the address of a nameserver
in a container on an `internal` network, and another container attached only to `internal`
networks, that network among them, and created without `--dns` nameservers

The container created without `--dns` nameservers resolves names through that
nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-FWD-WINDOWS-INTERNAL-NAMESERVERS**: On Windows, internal endpoints do not get --dns or dns nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* windows

*Concerns:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-CTR-NAMESERVER), [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-DAEMON-NAMESERVER) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-INTERNAL), [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS)

A Windows endpoint on an `internal` network does not get the nameservers set with
`--dns` or in the daemon's `dns` setting. A Windows container attached
only to `internal` networks does not resolve names through a nameserver on one of them.

<a id="DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS**: Without dns settings, the host's nameservers are queried from the host

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE](#REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE), [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge on a systemd-resolved host, queries skip 127.0.0.53 ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a host `resolv.conf` that names a nameserver by a valid IP
address, and a container that started with an endpoint on a user-defined network, has external
access and was created without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a
`dns` setting

The embedded resolver forwards to the nameservers in the host's `resolv.conf`, loopback
nameservers included. It queries them from the host's network namespace.

<a id="DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT-UPSTREAM**: With NetworkMode bridge on a systemd-resolved host, queries skip 127.0.0.53

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS), [DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT](#DNS-RESOLV-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-CONNECT) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` named only `127.0.0.53` when the daemon
started, and a container that was created without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon
does not have a `dns` setting, that has an endpoint on a user-defined network, from
its start, or after a connect while its `/etc/resolv.conf` had not changed since the
daemon wrote it, and whose `HostConfig.NetworkMode` is the default bridge, such as a
container that `POST /containers/create` created without a `NetworkMode`,
even when its `EndpointsConfig` names only a user-defined network, or the container
of a service task whose first network is not one of the Swarm's predefined networks

When `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` names a nameserver by a valid IP address, the
embedded resolver forwards the container's queries to the nameservers in that file, not to
`127.0.0.53`. When that file does not name a nameserver by a valid IP address, or does not exist,
the embedded resolver forwards the container's queries to `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, and queries
them from the host's network namespace. Then, when a nameserver that listens on port 53 at
`127.0.0.1` or at `::1` in the host's network namespace has a record for a name that the
embedded resolver does not have a record for, a query from the container for that name resolves
to that record's address.

<a id="DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-HOST-NAMESERVERS-NONE**: With no host nameserver, the embedded resolver uses 127.0.0.1 and ::1

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE](#REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE), [REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-UPSTREAM-SERVERS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a host `resolv.conf` that does not name a nameserver by a
valid IP address, because the file has no `nameserver` line with one or does not
exist, a broken symlink included, and a container that has external access, that was created
without `--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting,
and that started with an endpoint on a user-defined network or started attached only to the
default bridge and was then connected to a user-defined network while its
`/etc/resolv.conf` had not changed since the daemon wrote it, and a nameserver that
listens on port 53 at `127.0.0.1` or at `::1` in the host's network namespace and has a
record for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for

The embedded resolver forwards to `127.0.0.1` and `::1`. It queries them from the host's
network namespace: a query from the container for that name resolves to that record's address.

<a id="DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-NOT-REGULAR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-NOT-REGULAR**: A host resolv.conf that is a directory or a socket fails the container's start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A host resolv.conf that cannot be read as a file fails at the start, or at the first query ([RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE](#RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE))

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` is a directory or a socket, and a
created or stopped container that uses the embedded resolver

`POST /containers/{id}/start` for the container responds with a 4xx or 5xx status, with
a message that contains `is a directory` when the file is a directory, and
`no such device or address` when it is a socket.

<a id="DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-FIFO"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-HOST-RESOLV-FIFO**: A host resolv.conf that is a FIFO holds the daemon's start

*Observed from:* api · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* A host resolv.conf that cannot be read as a file fails at the start, or at the first query ([RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE](#RAT-DNS-HOST-RESOLV-UNREADABLE))

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` is a FIFO

When the daemon starts, its API does not respond before a process opens the FIFO for writing.
Once a process has written a resolv.conf to the FIFO and closed it each time the daemon opens
the FIFO, the daemon completes its start and its API responds.

<a id="DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-CONFIGURED-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS**: --dns nameservers are queried from the container's namespace

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE](#REQ-DNS-FWD-NAMESPACE) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose only `--dns` nameserver is `127.0.0.1`, a nameserver
that listens on port 53 at `127.0.0.1` in the container's network namespace, and one that
listens on port 53 at `127.0.0.1` in the host's network namespace, which give different
addresses for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for

The embedded resolver queries nameservers set with `--dns` from the container's
network namespace: a query from the container for that name resolves to the address that the
nameserver in the container's network namespace gives.

<a id="DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-CTR-NS**: The daemon's dns nameservers are queried from the container's namespace

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* The daemon's dns nameservers are reached from each container's namespace ([RAT-DNS-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-NAMESPACE](#RAT-DNS-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS-NAMESPACE))

*Applies to:* A daemon whose `dns` setting has the only nameserver `127.0.0.1`, a
container created without `--dns` nameservers, a nameserver that listens on port 53 at
`127.0.0.1` in the container's network namespace, and one that listens on port 53 at
`127.0.0.1` in the host's network namespace, which give different addresses for a name that
the embedded resolver does not have a record for

The embedded resolver queries the nameservers in the daemon's `dns` setting from
the container's network namespace: a query from the container for that name resolves to the
address that the nameserver in the container's network namespace gives.

<a id="DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-UPSTREAM**: After a live restore, the embedded resolver forwards to the same servers

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS](#DNS-HOST-EXTERNAL-ACCESS), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A running container that uses the embedded resolver, created without
`--dns` nameservers, on a Linux node whose daemon has `live-restore` true
and no `dns` setting, and a name of two or more labels that the embedded resolver
does not have a record for and that the nameservers in the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` have
records for

The daemon stops, the nameservers in the host's `/etc/resolv.conf` are replaced with
others that have records for that name with other addresses, and the daemon starts again. The
embedded resolver then forwards a query for that name to the upstream servers that it forwarded
to before the restart, and not to the nameservers now in the host's `resolv.conf`: the
name resolves to the addresses that the replaced nameservers give.

<a id="DNS-FWD-FAILOVER"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-FAILOVER**: No response, SERVFAIL or REFUSED moves the query to the next nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER](#REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER), [REQ-DNS-FWD-REFUSED](#REQ-DNS-FWD-REFUSED) · *Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container with two or more upstream nameservers, and a query for a name that the
embedded resolver does not have a record for, which the first of those nameservers does not
respond to, or answers with `SERVFAIL` or `REFUSED`, and for which the second has
a record of the query's type

The embedded resolver forwards a query to the next nameserver when the current nameserver does
not respond, or responds `SERVFAIL` or `REFUSED`. The query gets the second
nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL**: When every nameserver fails, the client gets SERVFAIL

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT](#DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* The rcode and flags of a response decide what the client does next ([RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT](#RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT))

When each nameserver that the embedded resolver forwards to does not respond, or responds
`SERVFAIL` or `REFUSED`, the client gets `SERVFAIL`.

<a id="DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-FAILOVER-TIMEOUT**: Over UDP, SERVFAIL comes after 4 seconds per silent nameserver

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-ALL-FAILED-SERVFAIL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

Over UDP, when each nameserver that the embedded resolver forwards a query to gives no response
at all, neither a DNS response nor an ICMP error, the embedded resolver responds
`SERVFAIL` to the client after 4 seconds for each of those nameservers.

<a id="DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-RESPONSE-RETURNED**: A successful or NXDOMAIN response goes to the client

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER](#REQ-DNS-FWD-ORDER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container with two or more upstream nameservers, where the second has a
different answer for the query than the first

The embedded resolver returns a nameserver's successful or `NXDOMAIN` response to the
client. It does not ask the next nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-OTHER-RCODE-RETURNED"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-OTHER-RCODE-RETURNED**: Any other rcode but SERVFAIL and REFUSED goes to the client

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Rationale:* The rcode and flags of a response decide what the client does next ([RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT](#RAT-DNS-RESPONSE-STEERS-CLIENT))

*Applies to:* A container with two or more upstream nameservers, where the second has a
different answer for the query than the first

The embedded resolver returns a nameserver's response with an rcode other than `NOERROR`,
`NXDOMAIN`, `SERVFAIL` and `REFUSED` to the client. It does not ask the
next nameserver.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-LIMIT**: The embedded resolver forwards to at most the first three nameservers

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-FAILOVER](#DNS-FWD-FAILOVER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container with upstream nameservers, set with `--dns`, in the daemon's
`dns` setting or in the host's `resolv.conf`, of which four or more are not a
nameserver `127.0.0.11` set with `--dns` or in the daemon's `dns`
setting, where the first three of those four or more do not respond to the query

The embedded resolver forwards the query to each of those first three, and not to the fourth of
them or to any later one.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF**: A --dns nameserver 127.0.0.11 is skipped

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-CTR-NAMESERVERS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A container whose nameservers set with `--dns` are `127.0.0.11` and
then a nameserver that has a record for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record
for

The embedded resolver does not forward to a nameserver `127.0.0.11` set with
`--dns`. A query for that name that the container sends once to `127.0.0.11` gets
the other nameserver's answer, and the container's loopback interface carries no other DNS query
from when the container sends it until the container gets the answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-DAEMON**: A daemon dns nameserver 127.0.0.11 is skipped

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS](#DNS-FWD-DAEMON-NAMESERVERS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon whose `dns` setting has `127.0.0.11` and then a nameserver
that has a record for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for, and a
container created without `--dns` nameservers

The embedded resolver does not forward to a nameserver `127.0.0.11` in the daemon's
`dns` setting. A query for that name that the container sends once to
`127.0.0.11` gets the other nameserver's answer, and the container's loopback interface
carries no other DNS query from when the container sends it until the container gets the answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY**: With 127.0.0.11 as the only nameserver, unknown names get SERVFAIL

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names ([DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)), With ndots 0 or invalid, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR ([DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)) · *Rationale:* When no configured upstream is left, a fallback would send queries to servers that nobody configured ([RAT-DNS-NO-UPSTREAM-LEFT](#RAT-DNS-NO-UPSTREAM-LEFT))

*Applies to:* Linux nodes with a container whose only nameserver, set with `--dns` or
in the daemon's `dns` setting, is `127.0.0.11`

A query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for gets `SERVFAIL`.
When the options in effect set `ndots` to 1 or more, a single-label A or AAAA query
gets an empty `NOERROR` response instead.

<a id="DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME**: A query for a name without records is forwarded upstream

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With ndots 0 or invalid, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR ([DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS), [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)

*Applies to:* A name and a query type for which the first of the querying container's upstream
nameservers has a record

The embedded resolver forwards upstream a query for a name that it does not have records for on
the querying container's networks, whatever the type of the query, other than an A, AAAA or MX
query for `<name>.<network>` where the querying container is attached to a network
named `<network>` and the embedded resolver has records for `<name>` on it, and other than a
PTR query for the reverse-lookup name of an address of an endpoint on those networks that has
names. A single-label A or AAAA query is the exception when the options in effect, which the
[resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf) section defines, set `ndots` to 1 or more. A
query for such a name and type gets that nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-MULTI-LABEL**: An unknown multi-label A or AAAA query is forwarded upstream

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A multi-label name that does not match any container, service or alias on the
querying container's networks, other than `<name>.<network>` where the querying
container is attached to a network named `<network>` and the embedded resolver has records for
`<name>` on it, and that the first of the querying container's upstream nameservers has A and
AAAA records for

The embedded resolver forwards an A or AAAA query for the name upstream. The query gets that
nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL**: An unknown single-label name is forwarded unless ndots is 1 or more

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux, windows

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), With ndots 0 or invalid, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR ([DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)

*Applies to:* A container on a Windows node, or a container on a Linux node whose options in
effect, which the [resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf) section defines, do not set
`ndots` to 1 or more, and a single-label name that the embedded resolver does not
have a record for and that the first of the container's upstream nameservers has A and AAAA
records for

The embedded resolver forwards a single-label A or AAAA query upstream when it does not have a
record for the name. The query gets that nameserver's answer.

<a id="DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS**: With ndots of 1 or more, an unknown single-label name is not forwarded

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS) · *Exact form:* [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names ([DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE)) · *Concerned by:* [DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL)

*Applies to:* A container on a Linux node whose options in effect, which the
[resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf) section defines, set `ndots` to 1 or more, and
an upstream nameserver of the container that has A and AAAA records for a single-label name that
the embedded resolver does not have a record for

A single-label A or AAAA query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for
gets a response without an address. The embedded resolver does not forward the query upstream.

<a id="DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR**: With ndots of 1 or more, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Exact form of:* [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names ([DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)), On a Swarm node, a rename leaves the records on other networks unchanged ([DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE](#DNS-NAMES-RENAME-SWARM-NODE))

*Applies to:* A container on a Linux node whose options in effect, which the
[resolv.conf](#container-dns-file-resolv-conf) section defines, set `ndots` to 1 or more

A single-label A or AAAA query for a name that the embedded resolver does not have a record for
gets an empty `NOERROR` response.

<a id="DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL**: With ndots 0 or invalid, an unknown single-label name gets an empty NOERROR

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL), [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME) · *Does not cover:* With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf ([DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS)), After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names ([DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL)) · *Concerns:* [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS), [DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO](#DNS-RESOLV-NDOTS-ZERO) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL](#REQ-DNS-FWD-EXTERNAL)

When the options in effect set `ndots` to 0 or to an invalid value, a single-label A
or AAAA query gets an empty `NOERROR` response when the embedded resolver does not have a
record for the name, as it does for an `ndots` of 1 or more. The embedded resolver
does not forward the query upstream ([moby/moby#53104](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/53104)).

<a id="DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-FWD-LIVE-RESTORE-SINGLE-LABEL**: After a live restore, ndots no longer affects unknown single-label names

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL), [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY), [DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR) · *Concerns:* [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS), [REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER](#REQ-DNS-LIVE-RESTORE-RESOLVER)

After the daemon restarts with `live-restore` true, the embedded resolver handles a
single-label A or AAAA query that it does not have a record for, from a container that kept
running, as it handles a query for a name of two or more labels, whatever `ndots`
the options in effect set. It forwards the query upstream. When it has no upstream server to
forward to, as for a container attached only to `internal` networks and created without
`--dns` nameservers, whose daemon does not have a `dns` setting, or a
container whose only nameserver, set with `--dns` or in the daemon's
`dns` setting, is `127.0.0.11`, the query gets `SERVFAIL`.

<a id="DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS"></a>

**Expectation (defect) DNS-FWD-DEFAULT-BRIDGE-SYSTEMD-NDOTS**: With NetworkMode bridge, the resolver takes ndots from systemd's resolv.conf

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS) · *Narrows:* [DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL](#DNS-FWD-INTERNAL-SERVFAIL), [DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY](#DNS-FWD-NAMESERVER-SELF-ONLY), [DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-NDOTS-ZERO-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS), [DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR](#DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS-NOERROR) · *Concerns:* [DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME](#DNS-FWD-UNKNOWN-NAME) · *Violates:* [REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS](#REQ-DNS-FWD-SINGLE-LABEL-NDOTS)

*Applies to:* A Linux node whose `/etc/resolv.conf` named only `127.0.0.53` when the daemon
started, where only one of that file and `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` sets an `ndots`, and a container whose DNS options are empty, that has an endpoint on a user-defined
network, from its start or after a connect, and whose `HostConfig.NetworkMode` is the
default bridge, such as a container that `POST /containers/create` created without a
`NetworkMode`, even when its `EndpointsConfig` names only a user-defined
network, or the container of a service task whose first network is not one of the Swarm's
predefined networks

Where only `/etc/resolv.conf` sets an `ndots`, the embedded resolver handles a single-label A or AAAA query that it does not have a record for as it handles a query for a name of two or more labels. Where only `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` sets one, the embedded resolver does not forward such a query upstream, whatever value that file sets.

<a id="container-dns-port-53-in-the-container"></a>

## Port 53 in the container

This section holds on Linux nodes.

<a id="DNS-PORT53-BIND"></a>

**Expectation (contract) DNS-PORT53-BIND**: A process binds port 53 while 127.0.0.11 still reaches the resolver

*Observed from:* ctr, task · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Refines:* [REQ-DNS-PORT53-SERVER](#REQ-DNS-PORT53-SERVER) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

A process in the container binds UDP and TCP port 53 on the wildcard address, or on
`127.0.0.11`, without an error. A query that the container sends to `127.0.0.11` does not
reach that process. The embedded resolver handles the query.

<a id="DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES**: Without the iptables command, queries to 127.0.0.11 get no answer

*Observed from:* ctr · *Depends on:* os-linux · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND) · *Needs:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-LEGACY-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-NFT-KERNEL), [DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-NFT-COMMAND), [DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT](#DNS-HOST-NFTABLES-NAT), [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with the iptables backend and `iptables` false, on a host
without the **iptables** command, and a running container with an endpoint on a
user-defined network

A DNS query from the container to `127.0.0.11` does not get an answer.

<a id="DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES-LOG"></a>

**Expectation (detector) DNS-PORT53-NO-IPTABLES-LOG**: Without the iptables command, the daemon logs the DNAT/SNAT failure

*Observed from:* log · *Depends on:* none · *Platforms:* linux

*Pins:* [DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND](#DNS-HOST-IPTABLES-COMMAND) · *Needs:* [NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC](network-common.md#NET-HOST-FIREWALL-PASSES-TRAFFIC), [NET-HOST-NETNS](network-common.md#NET-HOST-NETNS)

*Applies to:* A daemon with the iptables backend and `iptables` false, on a host
without the **iptables** command, and a running container with an endpoint on a
user-defined network

The daemon log contains `setting up DNAT/SNAT rules failed`.

<a id="container-dns-deliberately-not-asserted"></a>

## Deliberately not asserted

- The comments the daemon writes into `resolv.conf`, such as its header and its record of
  where `ndots` came from.
- The ports that the embedded resolver listens on.
- The firewall rules that the daemon programs in a container's network namespace: whether they
  exist, their content and names, and the hooks and priorities of their base chains.
